fields.name: active_time
fields.description: If this is a projectile then add -1 for active time

fields.name: update_targets_every_frame
fields.description: If active, then each model update it will re-evaluate the targets based on the current position. When off, it will do it once at the start and the targets won't change even if they move in / out of range.

fields.name: always_affect_self
fields.description: The launch unit will always be affected by the ability

fields.name: only_affect_target
fields.description: The ability will only affect the target unit and will not search near units

fields.name: min_range
fields.description: The (targetted) ability can't be used within this range

fields.name: targetting_aoe
fields.description: This is the area of effect to display when targetting

fields.name: passive_aoe
fields.description: This is the area of effect to display when ability has been ordered but not yet cast (like if unit has to move their to cast)

fields.name: active_aoe
fields.description: This is the area of effect to display when ability is currently active (has been cast)

fields.name: activation_effect
fields.description: This is an optional one-shot vfx to display when cast to acknowledge order given

fields.name: miscast_chance
fields.description: The unary chance of a miscast occuring

fields.name: miscast_explosion
fields.description: The boom-boom when miscasting happens

fields.name: special_ability_display
fields.description: When wind_up_stance has an animation added, and windup_time is set to greater than zero, this references a table where you can override effects in the animations metadata.   The effect metadata needs to be set to be set to ability_weapon and ability_aura.

fields.name: voiceover_state
fields.description: the state for the voiceover that's played when this ability is activated (if any)

fields.name: additional_melee_cp
fields.description: Melee Combat Potential that is added to any unit that has this ability/item (from table: main_units). Must be >= 0.0 or the game will crash on startup.

fields.name: additional_missile_cp
fields.description: Missile Combat Potential that is added to any unit that has this ability/item (from table: main_units). Must be >= 0.0 or the game will crash on startup.

fields.name: parent_ability
fields.description: Hack for spell browser in warhammer because designers want to put in specialised versions of abilities for certain characters. An ability with a parent wont show in browser, instead only parent is shown.

fields.name: spawn_proxy_vfx
fields.description: Vfx to show over each proxy decal when targetting spawn spell

fields.name: miscast_global_bonus
fields.description: Setting this to false stops miscast chance modifiers from affecting the ability

fields.name: composite_scene_group_on_wind_up
fields.description: Composite scene group we need to trigger when the ability starts winding up

fields.name: composite_scene_group_on_active
fields.description: Composite scene group we need to trigger when the ability actives

fields.name: use_loop_stance
fields.description: Entities will play a loop locomotion stance

fields.name: spawn_is_transformation
fields.description: If spawning a unit will mean the owner unit will be replaced by the spawned one

fields.name: spawn_is_decoy
fields.description: If spawning a unit the new one will be understood as a decoy of the owner one, the UI will show data for the owning one

fields.name: current_mana_moves_to_reserve
fields.description: If true the current winds of magic mana gets moved to the reserve

fields.name: spawn_shares_health_and_fatigue
fields.description: If spawning a unit will mean the transformed unit health and fatigue will be shared with the owning unit

fields.name: affect_siege_equipment
fields.description: If true affects siege equipment entities

fields.name: shared_recharge_time
fields.description: If provided will set this cooldown timer to all abilities on same group that have the field set

fields.name: intensity_based_activation
fields.description: Activates automatically when intensity is above 0 and deactivates otherwise

fields.name: autoresolver_usage
fields.description: How the ability is used in autoresolver calculations

fields.name: autoresolver_targets
fields.description: Number of targets the ability will hit if it is an aoe ability

fields.name: display_stops_when_display_expires
fields.description: If the ability shoots bombardment/vortex it's display will stop when the assets naturally expire (please make sure the display triggered doesn't loop infinite)

fields.name: autoresolve_cp_multiplier
fields.description: Multiplier for the CP values

fields.name: can_be_copied_to_transformation_unit
fields.description: If this ability can be copied to the connected transformation Unit

fields.name: audio_switch_casting_override
fields.description: If set, ability will use this switch for the modular casting

fields.name: audio_switch_ui_override
fields.description: If set, ability will use this switch for the modular UI

fields.name: ai_usage_template_group
fields.description: If set, ability will trigger on any template.

fields.name: cant_move
fields.description: Makes the unit unable to be given movement or attack orders (entities can still shoot, use abilities or react to melee).

fields.name: freeze_fatigue
fields.description: Makes the unit fatigue state 0 (=fresh) for duration of phase

fields.name: fatigue_change_ratio
fields.description: This is a scalar that changes the unit's fatigue (PER SECOND) relative to the maximum. For example, -0.25 will reduce it by 25% and 0.1 will increase it by 10%

fields.name: ability_recharge_change
fields.description: if the unit has abilities, their recharge will be changed by that amount (negative will reduce the time, positive will increase the time)

fields.name: hp_change_frequency
fields.description: In seconds, how often hp (hit point) change should attempt to be applied

fields.name: damage_amount
fields.description: Per entity, per frequency, what the amount of damage to apply. Note amounts under 4 do not work well on small unit sizes.

fields.name: max_damaged_entities
fields.description: Per damage/heal frequency, how many entities can we affect (negative is no limit)

fields.name: resurrect
fields.description: If ticked, when healing excess hit points will resurrect dead soldiers

fields.name: mana_regen_mod
fields.description: How much we add to the current recharge for mana per second

fields.name: mana_max_depletion_mod
fields.description: How much we add to the current value for max mana depletion

fields.name: imbue_magical
fields.description: Does this phase imbue the target with magical attacks?

fields.name: imbue_ignition
fields.description: Does this phase imbue the target with flaming attacks?

fields.name: imbue_contact
fields.description: Does this phase imbue the target with a contact phase when attacking?

fields.name: phase_display
fields.description: Add groups of visual effects

fields.name: is_hidden_in_ui
fields.description: If true, will not show up in UI

fields.name: replenish_ammo
fields.description: How much ammunition we want to replenish when phase starts (can be negative if we want to spend), this value is in percentage of unit max ammo

fields.name: composite_scene_group
fields.description: Composite scene group we need to trigger when the phase starts

fields.name: freeze_recharge
fields.description: Abilities on the target do not recharge while this phase is active

fields.name: heal_amount
fields.description: When HP (hit points) are healed, how much total should be changed, spread amoungst the entities

fields.name: barrier_heal_amount
fields.description: Each hp_change_frequency ticks, the barrier will heal by this proportion of max_barrier_health

fields.name: execute_ratio
fields.description: At or below this ratio of health the ability will instantly kill its target

In the midst of a bloodbath it's good to know that someone has your back.

The Dark Magic that holds these subjects together has failed. As the Necromantic energy flows out of them, nothing is left but a pile of iron and bones in the sand.
In the blasted desert of deepest Nehekhara, the dead rarely remain so. Those dragged back to screaming, clanking Unlife are bound forever to the Tomb King whose will they exist only to serve.
Crafted anew when an Everqueen ascends to the throne, the banner is a beacon of life and light.
The sky opens and a bolt of burning, pure Chaos black lightning hurtles towards the foe.
Tendrils of solidified darkness writhe outwards, draining the lifeforce from foes and renewing the caster’s own vigour.

Because you can never have too much.

Corpses bloated from spending too long at sea are like foul, decomposing balloons waiting to burst.
As the Vampires rip apart their victims they feast on the blood that spills forth – gaining strength and replacing lost stamina.
Possession of this orb enables the user to inexorably drag the foe into a turbulent vortex of pain and death.
Sotek's crawling, swarming allies surround the bearer, affording them further might and protection in the struggle to come.
A scorching ray of light blasts forth from the sky, putting the foe to flight or screaming, burning death - preferably the latter!
More than just a pile of rubble, these rocks also split armour apart, negating its protective capability.
The surprising ability to hold back death despite some seriously heavy opposition…

The presence of the hated Lustrian Blot Toad sends the merciless Ripperdactyls into a barely-controlled frenzy of extreme violence!
Command of this ability means never again having to run out of the Winds before the fight is well and truly done.
The more prominent the warrior, the better they are at stirring up subordinates to fight the ghastliest of enemies.
Knowing where the trap is - that's the first step in evading it.
There's no better defence than attack… preferably with this mass of whirling blades. Stay on the right side of it if you want to live!
The final word of the Old Ones to those not part of the Great Plan – short, clear and extremely deadly!
"Wade through blood and spill a bath-full more" is the code by which the legendary Carroburg Greatswords live and die.
Their lances gleam with such luminosity that the foe cannot see to adequately defend themselves against the Templars' devastating charge.
Steam must be let off from time to time, which leads to screaming, scalding death for any foe too close to the Emperor's Wrath during battle.
When you're up to your neck in corpses - and perhaps not all of them are properly dead - it's useful to be able to suppress your natural feelings of fear and dread.
The Empire's dark guardians do not retreat nor surrender, even when faced with seemingly insurmountable odds.
Steam Tank technology remains an inexact science, meaning they explode on occasion, and among the enemy's ranks if good fortune prevails!
Now you see them, now you don’t… and now you’re seeing double.
Like their huge, earth-boring equivalents, Warp-Grinders can turn solid rock into dust on a smaller scale, halting enemies’ movements by pulverising the ground beneath them.
The Siren’s voice is a fearsome weapon – should its sound reach an enemy’s ears, their lifeblood begins to violently rebel through every pore.
Warp-energy channelled directly into the ground causes the earth to tremble at a frequency that causes brains to rattle within skulls and bones to splinter!
Enemies who fight near a Bloodwrack Shrine find their minds twisted by the echo of the Medusa’s endless despair.
The pain of a shrine-bound Medusa permeates the battlefield, exuding a scent of suffering that invigorates those fighting alongside her.
Typically used to ensnare, immobilise and truss wild beasts, the Ravagers utilise their steel-wire nets against their foes to the same debilitating effect.
Khaine’s bloodthirst drives the murderous flock into a frenzied crescendo, enlivening and rejuvenating his foul manifestations.
The Death Squad’s unnatural head movements and bewildering upper-body agility mean their enemies often hit nothing but air.
The Phoenix's spiralling dive whips the Winds of Magic into a swirling vortex of magical flame.

Throwing bits of yourself at the enemy is either a sign of great determination... or singular stupidity.
Despite being an adolescent in Dragon terms, Gordinar’s breath blazes with the intense power of the sun itself.
Upon death, the potent arcane energies of the Phoenix erupt into a magnificent pyre.
The lurid fungus strapped to the front of this Pump Wagon explodes with immense force on contact with the enemy – much to the amusement of its Snotling crew!
The mere sight of a Phoenix lifts the spirits of the High Elves when darkness looms.

A true predator like Ceithin-Har shows no weakness when wounded, simply becoming even more of an impulsively deadly foe.

A Bladesinger’s dance may start as a mesmerising, graceful pirouette, but always ends as a violent maelstrom of slicing, gashing slaughter!
One too many Warp-fuel infusions have made the Hellion a volatile mutant indeed, allowing it to spontaneously discharge destructive magical vortices at will.
Lightning arcs across the battlefield, leaping from foe-to-foe with crackling fury until there are none left within the storm.
The caster calls down a mighty ball of lightning and hurls it - should the foe be struck they will surely be shattered!
All Lizardmen are roused at the wailing cry of the Troglodon, its eerie call stirring their savagery.
Those that look upon the Jabberslythe for too long will suffer insanity, even causing injury to themselves in desperation of escape.
Fuelled by looted wine, the Centigors strut and swagger with vulgar bravado to boost their own vigour.
These guardians of the most secret and sacred places can manipulate their environment to obscure themselves from foes.
So concentrated is the spurting vitriolic bile of this Jabberslythe’s wounds that it eats through solid armour to dissolve the flesh below.
This horrid creature bleeds stinking, vitriolic bile that spurts out from the slightest wound in great gouts of hissing back fluid.
A frequent gorging on the enemy’s battle lines leads to this one’s flesh flushing red as its wounds reknit themselves.

Crude though it may be, swiftly swooping in low to pepper the foe with rocks remains a most effective tactic.

With strange aeons even death may die...
"He who runs away lives to fight another day!" - so the foul, craven adage goes.
Snare-nets are lightweight but strong and covered in hooks. They are used by Gutter Runners to capture live prisoners.

Killing a Hell-Pit Abomination is never a simple matter; when it dies many fresh Skaven spawn to take its place.
With its last, shuddering death throes there is a chance that one or more of the foul beast's many hearts will restart.

'Better out than in' is a questionable maxim—particularly for the unfortunates caught in this deadly, reeking draught.
Where bodies fall, life springs once more, healing the wounded among the warriors of Nurgle.
Death is but a source of power, where the lifeblood of one may fuel the arcane wizardry of another.
Khorne blesses his warriors for every enemy slain, feasting on their suffering and screams.
The shrinemaster implores the fickle Chaos Gods for their aid, bestowing their dark blessings upon nearby champions.
Agonising pain is but a thrilling delight for Slaanesh, who revels in inflicting such torture on his foes.
All in the path of this murderous rampage will have little chance to react before being trampled into a fine red mist.

Use wisely, because just one careless puff will turn the Chaos Dwarfs' own ranks to cinders!

Birthed in the boiling blood of Hashut's burning sacrifices, this one radiates molten heat that weakens any foe close enough to attack.

Stick a Hobgoblin on a wolf and point them at the enemy, having first pointed out that if they retreat, *you'll* kill them, and they can be most effective when massed for a charge.

By which fear of death is exploited by the attacking force, enabling them to press their advantage and wipe the foe from the battlefield.
Those within sniffing distance of this enchanted pong find their own magical weapons practically useless while they remain there.
Unshakeable, unassailable strength of will can hold back anything, even death itself.
Down but not out… and never more dangerous. You'd be right to fear the wounded lion…
From every gap in the armour, bristling thorns burst forth to skewer unwary opponents.
A steady beat symbolises the staunch defences of the Bastion, a bulwark through which no enemy shall break.
Urged on by the pounding of drums, the Cathayan warriors fight untouched by fear, unleashing the fury of the Dragon on their foes.
This one's bark is at least as bad as their bite…
As the rising tempo reaches a crescendo, every man gives way to the rage of war, carrying their fury into every charge.
The piercing howl of the Incarnate Elemental of Beasts freezes the blood and fills all who hear it with mortal fear.
Before the enemy has seen the Lion in a single glance, its jade breath has burnt them to cinders.
The force of such a clash of fangs echoes out across the battlefield, forcing whole waves of men to their knees.
Those who cannot find shelter from this raging tempest of arcane power are sure to wither and break beneath its every wave.
Woe to the man or beast bearing this cursed mark, for the Lore of Yin has found an unwilling target and doom trails their every step.
Don't get anywhere near this silvery-blue flame as it gushes forth. Best not even look at it, in fact. Certainly do not touch it if you value your continued existence.
Who would have thought such a small, unassuming object could cause such overwhelming damage?
Every woven strand of net bears a powerful hex, draining every ounce of pace from the prey caught in its binds.
Distilled from the blood of Hag Queens, this evil brew drives imbibers into an ecstasy of destruction.

When activated, the Solar Engine radiates invigorating rays that stir nearby reptilians to energetic new heights of violence.
Death is not the end – it is only the beginning of the explosive devastation such a creature can cause.

Skinks tend to swarm around Kroxigor, encouraged by their awesome power. Kroxigor are likewise attracted to masses of Skinks, whose energetic movement and high-pitched sounds fuel their own battle-rage.
A roaring wave of magical energy explodes in all directions, scrambling the minds of all it does not decimate outright.
"All power to the engines – time is of the essence!"
As the Gyrocopter squadron speeds over the heads of the enemy, each pilot releases a single wing-mounted bomb onto targets below.
A vicious spear of steel explodes from the Airship with force, brutally impaling anyone and anything in its path.
With a sudden rush of piping hot steam, the Thunderbarge soars forward at speed, taking the battlefield by storm.
Being crushed or eaten may be a blessing when the alternative is choking on blood and puss as it slowly fills the lungs!
Dual axe-edges carve through foes, lashing out in a spiral of slaughter, and leaving nought but a bloody mess in their wake.
While the Land Ship's engines are undoubtedly marvels of technology, they're also known to be highly combustible…
Distance provides no safety; no matter how far the enemy runs, a sharpshooter's bullet will always find them.
Don't get any on your hands if you wish to keep them!
Imagine a rum so harsh and strong that only superior Dawi constitutions can bear it!
What was muffled, joyful frolicking becomes clearer as the bulges burst from their bloated host to find a new plaything.
Even the sturdy structures of artillery weapons are not half so hardy as the men who defend them.
When the normally-ebullient Nurgle cries, it is for His many children across this reality and all others.
Nurgle be praised! A revolting pus flower is a token of the Plague Lord's esteem; a gift of grandfatherly love, you might say, that his children might spread decay.
"Shrug off the petty blows of weaklings! Relish in mighty Grimnir's holy protection!"
A copious natural by-product of this noisome Colossal Squig's healthy digestion. Just don't step in it.
If it stays digested, anything this Colossal Squig eats is generally no longer considered a threat. Once it dies, all such considerations fall to the wayside.
Even simple destruction can be harnessed by a greater will. With Mangler Squigs, the metaphor is lost but the harnessing remains, in a terrifyingly literal sense.
"Get 'em flailin' an' confused. Makes fightin' more fun. Get 'em smoked. Makes 'em taste better."
Picky eaters are frowned upon amongst the Ogres. Picky fighters, however, are some of the deadliest amongst them.
When Orcs are determined to cleave something in half, very few things can stop them from doing so.
The walking embodiment of Winter itself, Yhetees channel the dark season's freezing weather to maim and kill their enemies.
A Wrathmonger's otherworldly storm takes on a decidedly worldly character in battle – bits of bone and gobs of flesh… and blood. So much blood.
The absolute carnage around Ogre mercenaries provides rich pickings for carrion-eaters, who do their bit for the war effort by taking more than their fill before battle is even done.
As if a raging Khorngor needs any reminders on, well, rage… though the dull fear of defeat and Khorne's displeasure provides a useful prod.
Running away from fear is what keeps you alive. Running towards fear is what makes you strong. The greatest Yhetees bring this wisdom with them down from the mountains.
That which is forged in Khorne’s own crucible moves with otherworldly speed to serve the cause of murder.
These Gnoblars love to joust each other when away from the battlefield, but will more-than happily practice on live foes to hone their, er, chops.
The fate of a Slaughterbrute is bound to its master. If its master lives, it kills at his behest. If not, it simply kills.
Maybe it's herd mentality, but in greater numbers, Gnoblars are a far more unified fighting force.
By means of the Lore of Shadows, the Wizard causes the enemy to be worn down by their own burdens, until they are enervated to a sorry standstill.
Spirits of the departed assail the Wizard’s foes, sapping their resolve and causing dread among their numbers.
With a mighty bellow, the spellcaster invokes Corvus the Crow Lord, summoning his servants to peck at the foe's eyes.
A salt-scented mist rolls in across the battlefield, corroding the enemy's resolve and shrouding the Asur with ethereal caress.
The innate hatred carried within a Preyton makes it despise itself almost as much as its foes, whose attacks are repaid with added enmity.
The terror is in knowing what its maw will do once it finally emerges.
Three snapping maws signal the Chimera’s unbridled destructive potential, with one harbouring the possibility of a fiery death.
An ever-shifting dermis of bright colours and hues turns translucent one moment, before running like molten wax to heal tainted flesh the next.
The very sight of a Merwyrm can provoke dread and hopelessness, its aura of crushing darkness even nullifying arrows and other missiles.
Whether sung in worship, or simply to embolden themselves, these riders’ songs are dreadful to the ear but pleasing to their god and fellow warriors.
For some war-prone creatures, the point where survival eclipses bloodlust has absolutely no in-between.
There is always one head more perverse and hateful than the other, pushing the Curs’d Ettin to move with violent, albeit lumbering zeal!
Some Curs’d Ettin retain enough intelligence in one head to recall secrets of their old tribal magic, allowing them to convalesce when under grave threat.
Some Curs’d Ettin retain enough intelligence in one head to recall secrets of their old tribal magic, affording them the power to nullify even the most potent magical armaments.
A gibbering head devolved into a drooling and wailing imbecile signifies a Curs’d Ettin in its most destructive personality. Avoid its club-like arms!
Seldom is a battlefield prowled by a Preyton not left strewn with corpses and dead creatures, mauled and trampled beyond any recognition.
Those who find the foolish resolve to charge the Merwyrm will find their approach hampered by an ocean’s chill that hits them bones-deep.
Rigorous practice over the Straits of Lothern drills the Swiftfeather Rocs in the auspicious wind-paths that husband their strength for devastating onslaught.
Reaching the seabed of their silent obsession, the Druchii straddle the peaks of euphoria. The journey down is tiring but impossible to abandon.
By the call of its mighty Sea Lords, the Asur fleet demonstrates why it is renowned as the greatest naval power in the world, its training superior to all others.
Pain is not a private thing for the followers of Slaanesh. They take pleasure in sharing its gift, hoarding it within themselves to grace whomever they chose.
This mottled grey fresh is shot through with pulsing veins reeking of corruption and rot – draw the Dread Maw’s blood at your peril.
A cornered Sea Elemental will often unleash lesser of its kind, discharging them like scalding geysers to mercilessly flay its assailants.
Disease seeps through the air around it. Malformed and nourished endlessly with concoctions of pure pox, even the healthiest of men wither with a single breath.
The visage of the Cauldron is enough to inspire even the most skittish of Skaven.
More than just a means of observation, the Celestial Hurricanum is a tool to invoke the wrath of the heavens upon the enemy.
The supernatural solution is often the best; weapons materialise in hands, allowing them to slice through flesh, soul, and consciousness.
The caster unleashes a vile disease that scours the battlefield in search of victims to infect and instantly petrify.
Those who ferry the Queen's exquisite throne once longed for her too...
Lahmians have grown skilled in the art of prescience to stay one step ahead of the agents who hunt them.
Usirian's scarabs prepare the dead for their existence as pure souls by stripping them of all fleshly remnants: a terrible fate to befall the yet-living.
When the Acolytes stewarding the Hurricanum achieve a perfect alignment, fiery comets come streaking out of the skies.
Reality itself melts into an unholy paste of vermin-made blasphemy whenever the cannon fires its profane lightning.
A minute adjustment of the Hurricanum's orrery can reduce formerly clear skies to a glowering rage.
Some souls do not deserve an afterlife. The only piece of it they see is Usirian's Icon engraved upon its most sacred Titans. After that – eternal nothingness.
Like their huge, earth-boring equivalents, Warp-Grinders can turn solid rock into dust on a smaller scale, halting enemies’ movements by pulverising the ground beneath them.
The Sands are where the Khemric Titans dwell. Reducing enemy ranks to dust widens their domain.
Sands lift in a blinding curtain as the Titan's enormous bulk emerges. Missiles fly awry and the swings of enemy warriors are reduced to choking fits and confused flailing.
When transfixed by its gaze, creatures feel their movements slow and their mind begin to unravel.
No formation can withstand the swing of these Giant-wielded hooked blades, either instantly disembowelling victims or leaving them reeling and gravely vulnerable to the next blow.
The presence of a Basilisk spoils the very air around it, sapping any creature in its vicinity of their ability to fight.
Once blood is tasted on the air, this Chaos Beast becomes frenzied, heightening its warp-given instincts and preternatural tenacity.
Only fools dare try to best those who bear the Plaguefather’s mark, most of whom lose their hope, sanity, and life trying to do so.
To an Ulrican, an enemy's stuttering step and fear-glazed eyes are no different than those of the wild beasts they hunt.
If slain, the incantations bound within a Khemric Titan are unleashed in howling vortices. Anyone caught in them crumbles to dust under the wrath of the millennial permanence undone.
The image of a legacy cursed many times over – a madman count, then Vlad von Carstein's flag of terror, now the symbol of Mannfred's indomitable hunger for power.
These Champions channel the foul power of Nurgle, granting unholy resilience to others that are deemed worthy by the Urfather himself.
Once the flesh of the host is torn, the diseases are unleashed. Flesh bubbles and melts away, spreading rapidly from creature to creature.
The Celestial Hurricanum constantly exudes magical power which – apart from fuelling its deadly manifestations – serves to replenish the arcane energies of its allies.
Flayerkin charge the enemy with eagerness to flay and kill.
They are but hosts, to serve a purpose.
Those who march beside the Hurricanum often report seeing visions of the imminent future, predicting the actions of the foe with uncanny accuracy.
"I be leader now, yes-yes! ‘Til I die-die, or you find someone better!"
The throne bears enchanted bowls of fresh virgin blood, from which Lahmians can scry the future.
Those that rush to attack this creature heedlessly will find themselves impaled upon the razor-sharp spikes that protrude from its carapace.
The weight of their profound suffering is only lightened by the promise of their eventual demise.
The wailing barks of these Siege Giants channel the hatred, pain and incoherent rage they feel for all other creatures.
The malodorous stink of decay eventually wears down even the hardest, most experienced combatants, dampening their spirits and resolve to press on.
The pure, unadulterated temptation that glorious perfection provides is as alluring as gold or the finest jewels.
The Changer's servants are shown a glimpse of their final victory, which imbues them with increased fighting vigour.
When the War Compass is so primed, even heavenly bodies are not outside its devastating reach.
The War Compass funnels deadly electricity from the heavens to sear and burn and smite the foe.
The more you kill, the more blood that you spill in His name, the more you will exsanguinate the enemies of the Blood God for His greater glory.
The exquisite kiss of the Dark Prince's three-tailed whip strikes the enemy with a delicious fury.
The spellcaster utters the vilest of phrases and belches forth an impossibly foul, poisonous cloud.
The most putrescent vapour fills the air, loosening lunches and bowels, and causing violent, crippling vomiting seizures in nearby foes.
A poisonous spurt of diseased gas and bile spews forth from the spellcaster's diseased lungs, drenching the enemy in vile, choking pus.
The spellcaster's corrupting touch puts their victims into a blissful, euphoric state for a short time, rendering them little able to move, let alone defend themselves.
A complex sigil is performed, transfixing the enemy with a shifting array of hallucinatory images that disjoint and befuddle, inviting their deaths.
With a twist of the hand, the spellcaster causes the bodies of their opponents to be consumed by coruscating blue flames.
A roiling tide of iridescent energy flows from the spellcaster, enveloping their enemies in a cone of searing magical flame.
When the land itself fights back, the enemy is petrified by its freezing touch, meaning the slightest gust will see them shatter into dust.
Gnoblars are at least as sneaky and trapsy as ordinary gobbos, as you may just find out!
Control the skies above the battlefield and you can be assured of success upon on the ground below – gravity is your ally, remember.
Ignition of this gunpowder mixture causes shavings to quickly scatter into a foul, painful cloud, leaving enemies vulnerable to the cut-and-thrust of close quarters combat.
When not fighting, Squealers can be put to good use conjuring up a fresh batch of magical mischief to lay the enemy low.
War is the crucible that melts all things.
Change isn't always welcome… or survivable, for that matter.
There must be balance in all things: dark and light, moon and sun, female and male.
There must be balance in all things: dark and light, moon and sun, female and male.
Kislevite warriors are inherently stronger than weak-hearted Empire-men, who know nothing of the hardship and strife of lives lived on the unforgiving steppes.
Through His endless pestilent blessings, the Plague Lord's followers thrive and surge forward when others would simply wither and die.
As the Daemon's courage falters, their mortal form crumbles and fades from this reality.
Once the Daemon's courage has failed them, they will fall back through the portal to the Chaos Realm whence they belong.

Become like the mountain: immovable, stronger over time, and nigh-on impossible to assail.
The higher you go, the further you can see, like the Dragons in flight above Cathay's harmonious landscape.
Others' fear is meat and drink to the Perfect Prince's Feasters of Pain.
When the bloodlust and frenzy are at their utmost levels, minor wounds are healed by the Blood God's towering, unassailable will.
The shrieking swords of the Horned Ones become more effective the longer the battle rages and the greater the number of piteous souls they harvest.
Only the most powerful magic-users can harness the Winds of Magic where they intersect and the power they generate is at its strongest.
Even the greatest foes can be laid low with terrible injuries, and the greater the damage done, the less able they will be to effectively continue the fray.
As the Skullcannon devours the helpless foe, their skulls feed its incessant hunger for fresh ammunition.
Attacking the Fly Lord's most faithful servants is made all the more difficult by the magical slime that slows enemy warriors and restricts their strikes.
The exquisite carnage sets the Hellstriders' souls on fire, girding and driving them further for the slaughter.
"Mmmm... meat... I can smell innocence at fifty yards!"
"Death is like a winter chill; No door can keep it from us; And summer yet may bloom again; Though ice be all upon us."
Reach into the realm of the Raven God and his blessings may just reach back.
The best plans are born at the brink of defeat, turning the tide when things seem most dire.
"Behold the festering hordes; from the gate they pour, ever undying in its shadow!"
"The flies! By the Gods, so many flies!"
Quench the soil in blood; every drop is but murderous motivation!
All fear the wrath of the storm-god Tor, striking foes down in a barrage of divine lightning!
Angry spirits inhabit discs of great power, spewing Tzeentchian fire on all those below.
Few can tolerate the scorching heat of Khorne's rage, leaving them vulnerable to the fiery winds that sweep from His realm.
Clouds of gas leak from toxic spores — a reeking restorative to all those aligned with the Lord of Decay.
An idol of Chaos, when lavished with attention, is sure to show off in the presence of such adoring followers.
Once the dreaded Wasting Sickness sets in, the muscles of the infected wither as their bones crumble to dust.
By means of the Lore of Shadows, the Wizard causes the enemy to be worn down by their own burdens until they are enervated to a sorry standstill.
At one with the frozen plains and snowy tundra of Kislev, wherever this one goes, they bring the icy heart of the Motherland with them.
A spray of sizzling silver slivers rain from the sky to impale the caster's enemy.
Just as a leech draws blood, the Wizard extends an ebon hand towards the chosen foe, sucking away their spirit through the tainted Lore of Death.
By which the Great Unclean One calls down a disgusting shower of putrid yuck to heal themselves and harm those foes unfortunate enough to be caught in it.
An icy carapace surrounds the Stonehorn, slowing the lumbering beast down further while adding a layer of natural armour to their defences.
The closer to monstrous foes the Bloody Fist is, the less likely it is to die. Truly a blessing from Khorne Himself!
This little bit of fiendish battle magick rains missiles straight back to the attacker, which, with a bit of luck, ought to put paid to further outbursts!
Loose threads of arcane power from nearby incantations are plucked from the breeze and woven into the barrier, reinforcing its strength.
Blisters bubble up from bulbous flesh, so assailants risk being doused in festering filth with every strike.
Submerged in filthy, stagnant water, wounds inexplicably knit together, and skin becomes whole. More curious are the grotesque boils that flourish and erupt, birthing a new sibling.
The Flag of the Blood Keep flashes violently; the Blood Knights run their enemies down.
Becoming more savage and frenzied the greater the scent and sight of blood.
These troops are emboldened when fighting, drinking and feasting together, although such ‘bravery’ is only temporary at best.
Goaded by Chieftains and enraged by intruders on their blood-grounds, Beastmen become consumed by a savage furore!
Cygors crave the souls of enemy Wizards more than anything else.
The Wizard casts an arcane net, created to hold the Great Deceiver himself. Any caught in its strands will struggle to act.
Balefire contains trace elements of Warpstone, so the burning braziers slowly drive mortal men to madness.
The unholy, never-to-be spoken words of this ancient grimoire cause the Winds of Magic to blow like a hurricane.
As if the enemy were caught in a blizzard or wading through treacle, the ice-cold aura slows any unit within range to a near-standstill.
As the final battle between good and evil looms, the flagellants ready to embrace death. The time is near; the end is nigh!
This depraved artefact, when held aloft, restores energy to those who swear fealty to its vileness.
Those who dare to stand against this profane monument will suffer from its corrupting influence, to their demise.
The ringing of the arcane bell atop the Corpse Cart inspires Undead minions to continue fighting, even when grievously wounded.
The Corpse Cart hardens shattered spirits and emboldens tattered bodies to ever greater acts of violence.
The truly hawk-eyed always hit their targets. Always.
Prickly gorse bursts from the ground around the caster's allies, protecting them from attack like a spiky, living shield.
At the spellcaster's command, nebulous nature spirits assail the foe, clawing with hands not nearly as insubstantial as they first appear.
What beauty and violence there is in the dance? A flurry of blades and a certain savagery of intent...
The wending and twisting of the Wardancers hardens their spirits and their bodies against would-be attackers.
The Wardancer threads and loops, contorting to create an ethereal fabric that turns aside arrows and bolts.
From the deepest, dankest forest depths a Treeman Ancient rises, charged with protecting its forest-kin from harm.
The minds of these warriors are turned over entirely to the defence of the Wildwood; nothing else affects them.
Not all Squigs have lasting usefulness. Some have a more fleeting... 'percussive' utility.
Those marked for death by the mighty Ranger or his crew may find their armour and shield of little practical use…
Somewhat surprisingly, even the deadliest Arachnarok feels protective of her brood, and can draw them to her at will.
The Gyrobomber is fitted with much larger ordnance than the Gyrocopter. Should the multiple payloads hit their intended target the results will be quite spectacular!
Clogging the senses with acrid, stinging smoke leaves an enemy completely vulnerable.
The Goblin Fanatics of Karak Eight Peaks eschew the use of balls with their chains, favouring shaved Dwarfs instead!
A touch of Bugman's Courage can keep a Dawi standing and fighting, a touch unsteadily, on their feet.
Greenskins are never gracious in victory. Wherever they can press an unfair advantage, they will!
Strong and tenacious, the Dawi’s hardy, passionate nature can be put to lethally good use on the battlefield.
If a Squig is not told what to bite, it will bite anything. Me, you, itself - anything!
Age, beard-length, and the courage that binds them; motivation, if any were needed, to fight on to the end.
Forming a wedge before the charge enables mounted Knights to smash through enemy lines, causing great disarray among their ranks.
Far more than allegiance or loyalty, true dedication to Lady and kingdom further empowers her Knights on the field.

On the battlefield, the Knights Errant are impetuous, eager to earn fame and honour in the thick of the fight. They charge boldly into the fray, heedless of danger and earning either great honour or a glorious death.

Thou shalt give unto thine glorious liege the taxes that he requires. Thou shalt labour all but feast days, and no more than a tenth-share shall you keep for kith and kin. Rejoice! For a Knight of Bretonnia provides your shield!
When going berserk, savage, barely-controllable warriors become savage, completely-uncontrollable warriors; best keep your distance!
When the Dark Gods bless the faithful assembled from atop their mighty battle-altars, loyalty is assured forevermore.
Dark figures move and twist within the magical miasma woven by the Fimir Balefiends as additional protection against the foe.
All it takes is the white-hot heat of battle to turn the issue of poor anger management into a violent advantage.
Each blow and every move only serve to make it a stronger and less-forgiving opponent.
Flies surround them, making combat even harder as the swarm buzzes into mouths, ears and other vulnerable orifices!
The Lady's blessing is a wondrous gift freely graced upon all Bretonnian subjects, should they but kneel and utter their devotion.
The Lady's blessing is a wondrous gift freely graced upon all Bretonnian subjects, should they but kneel and utter their devotion.
As Hysh gathers and swirls around the Luminark, it creates a becalming eddy that other magical winds struggle to penetrate.
The magical aura surrounding this unit protects allies from harm.
The Wizard infuses his allies with Light Magic, freeing them from the passage of time and speeding up their actions.
Lightning arcs across the battlefield, leaping from foe-to-foe with crackling fury until there are none left within the storm.
Bolts of cleansing energy fly from the Wizard’s hands, searing evil wherever they strike.
A pulsing nimbus of darkness envelops the Black Coach, making it sleeker and more resistant to enemies.
The Black Coach manifests gleaming scythes, as sharp as the night is dark.
The Hellcannon breaks its chains and rushes forwards. Increased movement speed.
The Gyrobomber is fitted with much larger ordnance than the Gyrocopter. Should the multiple payloads hit their intended target the results will be quite spectacular!
Sent mad by drinking fungus brew, Night Goblin Fanatics are released from their mobs as a twirling cyclone of destruction armed with a large ball and chain!
The Cairn Wraith and the skeletal steeds pulling the Black Coach are filled with unholy vigour.
Such is the strength within this warrior that when they strike it is sure to be a deathblow!
Some warriors care not for their own personal safety, and so work themselves into a whirlwind of destruction and mindless violence!
There are beings and creatures that can mend bone and knit flesh at an incredible rate. A mighty boon, but one stunted by fire.
The dead do not rest easily in the Old World. Those summoned by Vampires and Necromancers no longer have mortal concerns - they serve only their master's will.
The Dark Magic binding has failed. Both flesh and Necromantic energy slough off the subjects, leaving naught but dust.
If you see him coming run as fast as you can… not that it will do you any good whatsoever!
You really don't want to make them angry. No, *really*.
Shadows be thy cloak and darkness thy ally.
Sometimes less really is more; the souls of the fallen feed the engines of war.
Never make direct eye-contact with a Beastman lest it mark you out for a hideous, flesh-ripping demise.
In the midst of a bloodbath it's good to know that someone has your back.
The forest looks after its own.
